Point at a card at rest: React, Resolve and More fade in at its top right and nothing moves. The open card lifts with a hard shadow, shows its reply indented beneath the comment and ends with the reply box; turn off With replies to see a thread with none. Turn on With reactions to see a given reaction and the quick row under the open comment. In composing, Comment stays grey until there are words, as the hover cell shows once some are typed.

RFRed Fox9m ago

Lead with the recommendation; the finding can follow.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

MLMaya Lindqvist3m ago

Was it twice? The log says once, on the 14th.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

Walkers need a sign here before the meadow is gone.

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • For every thread, everywhere a thread shows: in the column beside the content, beside a bubble, in All comments and in the drawer. The same card is used in all of them.
  • For a comment being written (the composing variant), in the same place the thread will sit once it is sent.

When not to use

  • For a message from Pipeup itself ("Resolved", "Copied"): use cmp-inline-alert beside the comment control.
  • For a list of people: use cmp-list-row.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — the compact card at rest: the writer's avatar and name, how long ago, the comment's first lines and its reply count; its actions show on hover. The base class alone, no modifier class.
  • open — the thread opened: the card lifts with a hard shadow, shows its actions, every reply indented beneath the comment, and ends with a reply box with Cancel and Reply beneath it.
  • composing — a new comment: who you are with an invitation to add a name, the box with its placeholder, and Cancel and Comment beneath it; Comment stays grey until there are words.

Anatomy

Built from:

  • cmp-avatar, variant sm — the writer's portrait over their initials, at the start of the head line and of each reply.
  • cmp-icon-button, variant quiet — the actions at the card's top right: React (smiley), Resolve (check) and More (dots-three). The screen wraps More in a cmp-popover-menu (variant icon) holding Copy thread, and on your own comment Edit and Delete; the card itself holds no menu, so the panel that lists cards stays one level deep.
  • cmp-button, variants primary and quiet — Comment or Reply (primary) and Cancel (quiet), beneath the box.
  • cmp-text-field — the comment or reply box, a <textarea> with its visually hidden label.
  • cmp-chip, variant filter — a reaction someone gave, as a pressed pill with the emoji and its count, in the reactions row.

Own parts:

  • Root: <article class="ds-comment-card">; a <button class="ds-comment-card"> is never used: at rest the card's head is the control that opens it.
  • ds-comment-card__head: the first line: avatar, name, time and the actions.
  • ds-comment-card__name: the writer's name; ds-comment-card__time: how long ago, with the exact time in title.
  • ds-comment-card__actions: the icon buttons, hidden until hover, focus or open.
  • ds-comment-card__text: the comment's words, in the open card whole, at rest cut to a few lines.
  • ds-comment-card__count: the reply count at rest ("2 replies").
  • ds-comment-card__replies (with-replies): the replies in the open card, each a ds-comment-card__reply with its own head and text, indented beneath the comment.
  • ds-comment-card__box: the text field and, under it, ds-comment-card__buttons with Cancel and Comment or Reply.
  • ds-comment-card__you: in the composing variant, "You're Otter · add your name" with the name as a quiet button.
  • ds-comment-card__reactions (with-reactions): the row under the comment's words: the reactions given, each a pressed filter chip with the emoji and its count, and, while React is pressed, the quick row of five emoji as quiet buttons (ds-comment-card__quick).

Accessibility

  • At rest the head is a <button> that opens the thread (aria-expanded); the open card is a region named by its writer.
  • Actions are named by their action ("Resolve"), never the glyph; they can be pressed only while they show.
  • The box is a labelled text field: Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line, Esc cancels (with Undo for a few seconds).
  • Opening a thread puts the cursor in its reply box; Esc closes the thread and returns focus to what opened it.

Interaction

  • Hovering the card fades its actions in over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease; the card neither moves nor changes size (int-01, int-03).
  • Opening lifts the card by --ds-motion-lift and deepens its shadow over --ds-motion-settle; closing reverses it (int-04).
  • Hovering the card gives the commented content one slow, soft pulse, drawn by the page highlight, not by the card.
  • Comment and Reply are disabled until there are words; the change is a colour change over --ds-motion-quick.
  • React opens the quick row under the comment, fading in over --ds-motion-settle; choosing an emoji adds it to the reactions row (or counts it up) and the quick row fades out. The ⋯ opens the menu the screen wraps it in, as any popover menu does.
  • A sent reply arrives indented beneath the comment with a fade and the short drop over --ds-motion-settle; the reply box empties and keeps focus.
  • Under reduced motion nothing moves; actions appear in place (int-06).
  • A card arrives and leaves with a fade and a short drop over --ds-motion-settle: it carries data-ds-arriving for one frame and data-ds-leaving until it is hidden.

Content rules

  • The time reads "just now", "5m ago", "2h ago", "3d ago"; the exact time is in its tooltip.
  • The quick row offers five emoji: 👍 ❤️😂 🎉 🤔. A reaction reads as the emoji and a count: "👍 2".
  • The More menu reads Copy thread, Edit, Delete, in that order; Delete asks once more before it deletes.
  • The box's placeholder is "Comment or add others with @" or "Reply or add others with @".
  • Until a name is added, the writer is their animal: "Red Fox", "Otter".

Do and don't

  • Do keep the card narrow (about 280 px) so it sits in the column beside the text.
  • Do show a long comment's first few lines at rest, ending with "more".
  • Don't put anything beneath the words that would move them when the actions appear.
  • Don't nest replies: every reply is to the original comment.
Source: design-system/components/composite/cmp-comment-card/
